answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit meter bond and registers one work meter that emits a signed pulse per completed task. A falcon auditor samples the pulse stream and recomputes the delta between claimed and metered output; a delta above 2% burns the bond and seals the key. The k-th fake identity still needs its own meter, 25-credit installation plus 60 bond, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 and pay 25,000. Rented meters fail because the meter key binds to one identity and a borrowed pulse carries the wrong signature. An honest agent pays once and its delta stays near zero.
